properties.name: Levant Zone
properties.principle: Culture and history: the Levant in its narrow sense, as Starcom counts it (Cyprus, Israel, Jordan, Lebanon, Palestine and Syria, whole; Turkey's Hatay left out). Its Sectors follow the land's physical belts (the coast and its mountains, the Orontes and the Beqaa, the Damascus basin and the Hauran, the desert, the Euphrates, the Jordan rift and the highlands either side of it, and the island) and never a contested line: lines run along the Jezreel valley, the rift's escarpments, the Hermon and Anti-Lebanon crest, the Yarmouk and the Euphrates, so the rift holds both banks of the Jordan and the Golan lies with the Hauran. No Sector names a state or says who a territory belongs to.

declared.name: Desert margin (east of Salamiyah to Lake Assad)
declared.note: The Syrian Desert's edges with the settled lands (the Aleppo plateau, the Damascus basin and Hauran, the Transjordan Plateau, the Euphrates valley) are the desert margin: a band tens of kilometres wide where rain-fed farming gives way to steppe, drawn here by judgement east of Salamiyah, Dumayr, the Jabal al-Arab, Zarqa, Qatrana and Ma'an, and south of the Euphrates' bluffs.

declared.name: Hauran plain (Wadi az-Zaydi to the Jabal al-Arab)
declared.note: Between the Yarmouk's headwaters by Daraa and the foot of the Jabal al-Arab the Hauran is an open basalt plain with no ridge or river across it; the line between this Sector and the Transjordan Plateau follows the Wadi az-Zaydi toward Bosra and is then drawn straight. It is a band, not a feature, and it neither follows nor stands for the Syria-Jordan border.

declared.name: Desert margin (all round)
declared.note: The Syrian Desert's edges with the settled lands (the Aleppo plateau, the Damascus basin and Hauran, the Transjordan Plateau, the Euphrates valley) are the desert margin: a band tens of kilometres wide where rain-fed farming gives way to steppe, drawn here by judgement east of Salamiyah, Dumayr, the Jabal al-Arab, Zarqa, Qatrana and Ma'an, and south of the Euphrates' bluffs.

properties.name: Coastal Levant
properties.character: The Mediterranean shore and the mountains behind it, from the Turkish line to the Jezreel valley: the Syrian coast under the Jabal Ansariyah, Mount Lebanon, and Jabal Amel with its southern continuation, the Galilee.
